title: Saturation
description: Burn-rates and retention-vs-disk headroom for the single VPS. Text guidance only — NO retention values are changed by this board. Home folder: Cogito — one folder holds boards and alert rules.

panels.title: Retention vs disk — the math (read before touching anything)

options.content:
Facts (verified in git): Loki retention 30d (`loki_retention_days: 30` → `retention_period 720h`, infra/ansible/observability.yml) · Prometheus retention 15d (`--storage.tsdb.retention.time=15d`, infra/prometheus/prometheus.yml) · single VPS disk 38GB.

How to read this board: panels 2–4 show the *burn rate* (bytes/s filling disk, bytes/s draining memory, CPU saturation + load). Headroom math = (free bytes today) ÷ (burn bytes/day) = days until full. Compare that number against the retention horizons above: if disk fills faster than 30d of Loki + 15d of Prometheus + Docker overlays + backup temp space, the host dies before retention ever matters.

If the math says we are short: options are (a) grow the disk, (b) cut cardinality at the source (cAdvisor `--disable_metrics=disk,diskIO`, fewer log lines), or (c) shorten a retention window. Option (c) needs OPERATOR APPROVAL on evidence — retention is a durability/compliance promise, not a tuning knob; this board's job is to produce the evidence (screenshot the burn panels), not to make the cut. No retention value is changed by any panel or alert here.

panels.title: Disk burn rate (bytes/s filling)
panels.description: Negative deriv of rootfs free bytes over 6h, so positive = filling. Multiply by 86400 for bytes/day headroom math. Saw-tooth from logrotate/nightly-prune is normal — act on the sustained baseline, not spikes.

panels.title: Memory burn rate (bytes/s draining)
panels.description: Negative deriv of MemAvailable over 6h, so positive = draining. Sustained drain + growing swap (Infra board panel 6) = leak or growth to size before it OOMs.

panels.title: CPU saturation + load
panels.description: CPU % (non-idle) against load averages. Load persistently above core count with low CPU % = uninterruptible (iowait) pressure — check Infra panel 5 (CPU by mode).
